h1: The 6 Best Hedge Trimmers Under $50 for Small Yards, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Hedge Trimmers Under $50: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 hedge trimmers under $50 scored on blade length, branch capacity, motor power, battery setup, vibration and ease of use.
summary: The BLACK+DECKER 17-inch corded trimmer is the one to buy for a yard with an outlet in reach, with a dual-action blade, a 3.2 amp motor and a 5/8 inch cutting capacity. The OGERY is the best cordless pick with two 21V batteries, the Nicklaua tilts its head for awkward angles, and the VERVEWAVE is only worth it if you already own DEWALT 20V batteries.
intro: Under $50, the question is not which hedge trimmer is best. It is which kind of trimmer your yard can use. A corded one gives unlimited runtime but a leash, a cordless kit gives freedom but a limited battery, and a bare tool that needs your own battery costs less than it appears. Buy the wrong type and the specifications stop mattering. Count the cord, the battery and the charger as part of the price before comparing models.

So this ranking sorts by power type first. We reviewed six hedge trimmers under $50 from their listings, comparing blade length, motor rating, branch capacity, battery arrangements, head angle and vibration features. Capacity figures like 5/8 inch describe twigs, not branches, and these trimmers suit shaping, not heavy pruning.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 17-Inch Corded 3.2 Amp Hedge Trimmer
products.verdict: A 17 inch dual-action blade and 3.2 amp motor that cuts up to 5/8 inch, with reduced vibration.
products.description:
The BLACK+DECKER corded trimmer has a 17 inch dual-action hardened steel blade, a 3.2 amp motor, a cutting capacity of up to 5/8 inch and a reduced-vibration design.

It ranks first because it has the longest blade here, so you cover more hedge per pass, and corded power never fades. A dual-action blade cuts on both sides, which lowers vibration compared with single-action blades and makes the tool easier to hold. It beats the 16 inch BEHT100 on reach, and it outruns the cordless models on sustained power.

Buy it when an outlet or extension cord reaches your hedge. The cord limits where you can work, and you must keep it out of the blade path.
products.idealFor: Homeowners with an outlet nearby who want the longest blade.
products.skipIf: Your hedge is far from any outlet.

products.name: OGERY 21V Cordless Hedge Trimmer and Grass Shears
products.verdict: Two 21V batteries, an 8.9 inch hedge blade, speeds up to 2000 RPM and a grass shear conversion.
products.description:
The OGERY is a 21V cordless 2-in-1 with two batteries included, an 8.9 inch hedge blade, speed of up to 2000 RPM and a grass shear conversion.

It ranks second because two batteries are the practical advantage: you can swap one while the other charges, which doubles your working time on a larger hedge. The grass shears add edge trimming at no extra cost. It has a much shorter blade than the 17 inch corded trimmer, so you make more passes, and it is slower on thick growth.

Choose it for cordless shaping with a spare battery and grass shears. An 8.9 inch blade suits shrubs, not long hedges.
products.idealFor: Gardeners who want cordless shaping with a spare battery.
products.skipIf: You trim long hedges and want fewer passes.

products.name: Nicklaua Cordless Hedge Trimmer and Grass Shear 2-in-1
products.verdict: A 9 inch hedge blade, a 5.3 inch grass blade and a head that rotates to 15, 30 and 45 degrees.
products.description:
The Nicklaua has a 9 inch hedge blade, a 5.3 inch grass blade, a head that rotates to 15, 30 and 45 degrees and a no-load speed of 1500 rpm.

It ranks third because the rotating head helps with the awkward cuts that fixed heads handle badly: the tops of hedges, tight corners and low borders. A 9 inch blade is a little longer than the OGERY's 8.9 inch. At 1500 rpm no-load it is slower than the OGERY's 2000 RPM, which shows on thicker twigs. The listing gives no battery details.

Pick it when you spend more time shaping tight corners and borders than cutting long runs. Check the battery and charger in the box before ordering.
products.idealFor: Shrub and edge trimming where blade angle matters.
products.skipIf: You need speed for thick growth.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 16-Inch 3.0 Amp Compact Hedge Trimmer BEHT100
products.verdict: A 16 inch, 3.0 amp corded trimmer with a 5/8 inch capacity and a cord retention system.
products.description:
The BEHT100 has a 16 inch blade, a 3.0 amp motor, a cutting capacity of up to 5/8 inch and a cord retention system.

It ranks fourth because it is a near twin of the 17 inch model with a little less reach and a little less motor, so you give up about an inch of blade and 0.2 amps for little saving. The cord retention system is a practical design touch: it clips the extension cord to the handle so it does not pull free mid-cut.

It is enough for a short run of shrubs by the front door, close to an outlet. For a longer hedge, take the 17 inch model.
products.idealFor: Small yards and front-step shrubs with an outlet close by.
products.skipIf: You have long hedges to cover.

products.name: Supleap 2-in-1 600W 21V Cordless Hedge Trimmer
products.verdict: A 600W 21V trimmer with a battery charge display, double-sided multi-angle blades and a shock-absorbing grip.
products.description:
The Supleap is a 600W, 21V 2-in-1 trimmer with a battery charge display, double-sided blades that adjust to several angles and an anti-slip, shock-absorbing grip.

It ranks fifth because it adds a battery display and a vibration-damping grip to a typical cordless 2-in-1. Knowing the battery level lets you plan a hedge instead of running dry halfway. It sits below the OGERY and Nicklaua because the listing gives no blade length, speed or battery count.

Choose it for cordless work where you want to see the battery level and adjust the blade angle. Without blade specs, check the listing before buying.
products.idealFor: Cordless users who want to see battery level and adjust blade angle.
products.skipIf: You want stated blade length and speed.

products.name: VERVEWAVE Cordless Hedge Trimmer for DEWALT 20V Battery
products.verdict: A 2-in-1 trimmer that runs on DEWALT 20V MAX batteries, with battery and charger not included.
products.description:
The VERVEWAVE is compatible with DEWALT 20V MAX batteries, which are not included, and does not include a charger. It is a 2-in-1 with grass shears and a hedge trimmer and an upgraded copper wire motor.

It ranks last because the price looks low only if you already own a DEWALT battery and charger. It is a third-party tool built around another brand's battery, so fit and support depend on the seller. The 2-in-1 shape is useful for light work.

It only makes sense if a DEWALT 20V MAX battery and charger are already in your garage. If you do not, a complete kit like the OGERY costs about the same.
products.idealFor: People who already own DEWALT 20V MAX batteries.
products.skipIf: You do not already own a compatible battery.

whatMatters.detail: A corded trimmer never runs out of power, and an extension cord limits where you can work. A cordless unit is free of the cord but limited by battery. Choose by the distance from the nearest outlet to the farthest hedge. Measure the walk from the nearest outlet to the far end of the hedge, and add a cord only if it is rated outdoors.

A 17 inch blade covers more hedge per pass than an 8.9 inch one, which saves time on long runs. Shorter blades are easier to control on small shrubs. Check the listed blade length, and match it to the size of your hedge. Longer blades also cost weight, so a heavier 17 inch unit tires the arm sooner than a compact 8.9 inch one.

A rating of 5/8 inch means the blade will cut twigs up to that thickness, not branches. Anything thicker needs loppers or a saw. Check the capacity before buying, and expect to prune thick wood separately. Anything near that limit will jam or stall the motor, so treat the number as a ceiling for green growth.

A dual-action blade moves both sides against each other, which cuts more smoothly and reduces vibration. Single-action blades vibrate more. Look for dual-action in the listing, especially if you trim for long periods. The Nicklaua and BLACK+DECKER pages list the features you can verify; if the blade action is unlisted, assume single-action.

Some cordless trimmers include batteries and a charger, while bare tools do not. A kit with two batteries lets you swap while one charges. Check exactly what is in the box, since a missing charger changes the price. The VERVEWAVE leaves out both battery and charger, and that mismatch is the most common surprise in this price tier.

faq.q: Can these trimmers cut thick branches?
faq.a: No. The BLACK+DECKER models cut up to 5/8 inch, which is twigs. For anything thicker, use loppers or a pruning saw. Use a hedge trimmer for shaping new growth. Shaping a hedge means cutting new shoots, not woody stems.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake?
faq.a: Buying a bare tool and forgetting the battery. The VERVEWAVE has no battery or charger, so the real price depends on what you already own. An OGERY includes two batteries. The 8.9 inch OGERY blade is a poor match for older, thicker hedges.

faq.q: Is a cordless trimmer worth it over a corded one?
faq.a: If your hedge is far from an outlet, yes. The OGERY's two batteries let you swap while charging. If the hedge is near the house, a corded model like the BLACK+DECKER 17-inch gives longer reach. The Supleap's charge display shows runtime, which is the answer a corded model never needs.

Wear eye protection and gloves, and keep the cord behind you on corded models. Work in sweeping arcs, and never trim in rain. The BEHT100's cord retention helps keep the cord clear. Check that guards cover the blade before storing.

faq.q: How do I maintain a hedge trimmer?
faq.a: Wipe off sap and debris after use, and apply a light oil to the blades. Store the tool dry, and for cordless models, store the battery indoors. Dull blades tear the foliage. Do not wash the blade with a hose.

faq.q: Do the grass shear attachments work on lawns?
faq.a: They suit edges and small patches, not a whole lawn. The Nicklaua's 5.3 inch grass blade and the OGERY's shear conversion are for trimming borders. Treat both as edging tools; a hedge trimmer motor lacks the power to cut a lawn evenly, so keep a mower for the main grass.

finalTake: The BLACK+DECKER 17-inch corded trimmer is the best buy if an outlet reaches your hedge, because it has the longest blade and constant power. The OGERY is the best cordless choice with two batteries, and the Nicklaua is better for awkward angles. Skip the VERVEWAVE unless you already own DEWALT batteries.
